marc:datafield.marc:subfield: 金門曆史建築導覽. 第二冊 | Jinmen li shi jian zhu dao lan. Di er ce

Kinmen has long placed great importance on clan culture, a tradition deeply rooted in Confucian values of filial piety. This form of social and familial organization has been highly respected by the people of Kinmen throughout history. The island is home to over 190 ancestral halls belonging to various family surnames, of which 11 have been officially designated as historic buildings. Additionally, there are 9 temples associated with Minnan folk religion, 1 Christian church, and 4 tombs, which are the burial sites of founding ancestors or locally renowned figures who made significant contributions. Due to its strategic role as a military outpost for over 40 years, Kinmen also preserves numerous military heritage sites, including bunkers, fortifications, and monuments. There are also educational institutions that were closely tied to the island's military functions—these military-education sites represent a unique blend of education and defense, reflecting Kinmen’s historical role. These architectural sites are considered some of Kinmen’s most valuable cultural assets, and this book primarily focuses on describing them. In cases where the owner of a building or their personal background had a particularly significant influence on the structure, the text begins with a brief analysis of the historical and social context, to help readers better understand the connection between the individual, the era, and the building itself
